## Objective
- Complete and validate the existing Snake-like property puzzle as a local multiplayer game for up to four players taking turns in rounds.

## Requirements
- Support 1–4 players and round-based turns.

## Decisions
- Players share the city board and take one move per turn; each game lasts 24 rounds.
- Players have separate snakes, cash, and properties; coins earn cash, properties charge rent, and stairways provide shortcuts.

## Work State
### Completed
- Wired player-count selection, visual/accessible selected state, and chosen player count into start and restart behavior.
- Updated wallet and goal labels for the active player; made player 2’s start position distinct from the original player’s.
- Updated help, controls, overlay, and footer to explain one move per turn and 24 rounds.
- Verified `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`; browser-loaded the game and confirmed selecting four players starts a game with four player chips.

### Active
- Validate turn rotation, round progression, purchases, cash/rent/property updates, and final standings in browser gameplay.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test turn rotation and round advancement for 1–4 players, including crashes and purchases.
2. Test rent transfers, cash displays, victory at $300, and final standings after round 24; fix any issues.
3. Investigate the initial browser console error if needed; it currently reports only a missing `/favicon.ico` (404).

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Multiplayer logic, player selection, turns, economy, and game completion.
- `index.html`: Game UI, player selection, controls, and help text.
- `style.css`: Board and responsive game layout.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser testing confirmed four-player selection and startup; gameplay progression has not yet been tested.

- Complete and validate the existing Snake-like property puzzle as a local multiplayer game for up to four players taking turns in rounds.

## Requirements
- Support 1–4 players and round-based turns.

- Players share the city board and each take one move per turn; games last 24 rounds.
